summary: Swept my 4 files for POSIX/Linux code (unistd/fcntl/sys, g_spawn/GSubprocess, g_unix_*, gdk_x11/GDK_BACKEND, '/' paths, file://, getenv/HOME, Linux wording such as PulseAudio/PipeWire/pactl/Wayland/X11/run-radios.sh/flatpak, font-family in C-string CSS, g_time_zone_new_identifier/get_identifier). None was left. header_status.c already uses radios_time_zone_new() with a UTC fallback and radios_date_time_format() for %Z. Its C-string CSS (stream-light colours) has no font-family. Its theme file assets/themes/header-status.css has no font-family either and is not my file. autodj_settings.c needed no change. The "sunucu" texts in header_status.c mean the Icecast stream server, not a Linux audio server, so they stay. I made two fixes under D2 (industrial quality). (1) playout_ui.c: every engine snapshot (~266 KB) and receipt window (~112 KB) moved from the UI-thread stack to the heap. Compiling with -Wframe-larger-than showed 15 functions with stack frames of 112-534 KB. install_plan, with choose_pool inlined, was 534 KB, and nested GTK callbacks can stack more than 1 MB (the Windows default stack is 1 MiB). After the change no function has a frame over 16 KB. (2) settings_sync.c: values read from the shared desktop_preferences database document are now type-checked. All 4 files compile cleanly once each with the strict ENV_CLOUD recipe (-Werror, -c only). As instructed, I ran no tests and nothing under Wine.
api: No public API or contract changed: all headers and the radios_playout_ui_*, radios_header_status_*, radios_autodj_settings_new and radios_settings_* signatures are unchanged, and no Turkish UI text changed. New private static helpers in playout_ui.c: receipts_take(p, &count) returns a g_new'd array of RADIOS_AUDIO_RUN_MAX_RECEIPTS receipts that the caller g_free's; audio_snapshot_new(engine) returns a g_new0'd, filled RadioSAudioSnapshot that the caller g_free's; choose_pool() is now a thin wrapper around choose_pool_snapshot(p, plan, audio, error). New private helpers in settings_sync.c: a type-safe member() and object_member().

Grepped all 4 files for unistd/fcntl/sys/, g_spawn, GSubprocess, g_unix, gdk_x11, GDK_BACKEND, file://, getenv, HOME, Pulse/PipeWire/pactl/Wayland/X11/flatpak/run-radios, font-family, g_time_zone_new_identifier/get_identifier, fopen/open/stat, long/off_t: nothing to convert.

Final strict compile of all 4 owned files (std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 -DUNICODE -D_UNICODE, ENV_CLOUD pkg-config cflags, -c only) into /opt/radios-port/work/c-ui-sweep-p5/: autodj_settings.o, header_status.o, playout_ui.o and settings_sync.o all built with exit code 0, no errors and no warnings. Compile helper: /opt/radios-port/work/c-ui-sweep-p5/cc.sh.
Checked that radios_audio_engine_snapshot() memsets its output and that the copyright APIs take const pointers and copy them, so heap buffers are safe and behaviour is unchanged.
Not run, as instructed: no linking, tests, probes or Wine runs.
industrial_fixes: playout_ui.c: RadioSAudioSnapshot (~266 KB: 66 decks plus 2 x 64 device entries of 513-byte names) was a stack local in 13 places: route_adjuncts, the three branches of choose_pool, install_plan, replace_remaining_commit, remove_future_entries, replacement_ready, the preparation callback, prepare_start_origin, the scope start, live_step_end_current and deck_metadata. All now use heap snapshots. install_plan alone had a 534 KB frame (choose_pool inlined), and chains such as poll -> install_plan -> choose_pool could pass 1 MB on the GTK thread, overflowing the Windows default 1 MiB stack in any exe not linked with --stack 8 MiB. Where only a deck generation or one deck is needed, it is copied out and the snapshot freed at once. replacement_ready's early returns became a refusal variable so the buffer is always freed. prepare_start_origin frees the snapshot on its invalid-player return.

playout_ui.c: the four RadioSAudioRunReceipt receipts[2000] stack arrays (~112 KB each) in capture_history (which runs on every poll tick), prune_observed, the resume path and radios_playout_ui_take_completed now use one heap buffer per call (receipts_take). controller_copyright's two 12 KB copyright window arrays became one heap buffer of exactly count entries, reused for the adjunct windows.

settings_sync.c (remote_loaded): values from the shared desktop_preferences document were read with json_object_get_int_member/json_object_get_object_member without type checks. A null or non-integer member made json-glib raise a critical (fatal under G_DEBUG=fatal-criticals in tests) and return 0. A negative or >32-bit value silently wrapped when cast to guint (e.g. 4294967397 became 101, which passes validation). Now a member that is not an integer between 0 and G_MAXUINT keeps the local value, and a 'ui'/'audio_panel' entry that is not an object is ignored. Range validation stays in radios_ui_preferences_save / radios_preferences_audio_save.
requests_for_other_areas: c-ui-sweep (other chunks: owners of src/ui/player_rotation.c, src/ui/player_scope_execution.c, src/ui/preferences.c): each of these files has 2 stack locals of type RadioSAudioSnapshot (~266 KB each; total frame sizes not measured). Move them to the heap as done in playout_ui.c (g_new0 + radios_audio_engine_snapshot + g_free). Compiling with -Wframe-larger-than=65536 lists them.

build-system (CMakeLists.txt / cmake/*): many tests (tests/test_runner.c 28, tests/test_audio.c 21, tests/test_playout_ui.c 14 and about 30 more files) keep RadioSAudioSnapshot (~266 KB) or RadioSAudioRunReceipt[2000] (~112 KB) on the stack. Per D7, make sure every test and tool executable, not only RadioS.exe, links with -Wl,--stack,8388608.
open_issues: playout_ui.c runner_command(): when RESUME is refused while the MAIN output reopens after a pause/seek flush, it retries for up to 250 ms on the GTK thread with g_usleep(10 ms) (about 15.6 ms per sleep on Windows' default timer). The 250 ms window was tuned for the Linux reopen time ('about 0.2 s'). A WASAPI shared-mode stream reopen may take longer on some drivers, in which case RESUME returns UNAVAILABLE to the operator. Not changed (it is a timing policy, and the engine-side behaviour belongs to the audio area). Check on the user's PC with real devices.
Not done, as instructed (write-only pass): no linking, tests or Wine runs. header_status.c and autodj_settings.c were only grep-swept and compiled, with no behaviour review beyond that.

U+23ED (⏭) in a playout_ui.c error message is not in Inter 4.1 (gtk-windows-runtime.md glyph audit). It relies on the CSS/Pango font fallback list (Segoe UI Symbol), which the font/theme area owns. Nothing to change in this file.
